text: For single-photon detection at 1550 nm, superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) beat InGaAs SPADs in efficiency, dark-count rate, and timing jitter. What is their main practical drawback?
choices: They only work at visible wavelengths
They have very low detection efficiency (15–25%)
They have very high dark-count rates
They require cryogenic cooling, adding cost and complexity
explanation: SNSPDs deliver 90–98% efficiency, sub-cps dark counts, and <3 ps jitter, but must operate at cryogenic temperatures (kW-scale 4 K cooling), which is their chief disadvantage. The low efficiency (15–25%) and high dark counts actually describe the room-temperature SPAD, and SNSPDs span 400–2000 nm, not just visible.
